meta.title: Required API surface for the HybridCloudWorks website
meta.purpose: Defines the backend contract used by the frontend: only routes with current consumers belong in the implemented surface, while intentionally unavailable integrations remain explicit.

derivedFrom.method: static extraction of firebase/firestore, firebase/auth, firebase/storage usage and postJSON/authedFetch call names from frontend/src; hook indirection (useFirestore.js) resolved by call-site scan

meta.constraint: azureConfig.js: the browser must not instantiate a Cosmos DB data-plane client or receive a Cosmos access key. Every direct Firestore touch below therefore needs a Functions endpoint.

rpc.description: Named functions the frontend already invokes through lib/api.js (postJSON/authedFetch). These are backend-routed today; the port is implementing them as Azure Functions HTTP handlers under the existing auth middleware. Source: Site-Main functions/cms-functions.js (105 exports) and labs-functions.js.
rpc.authModel: Entra bearer token via requireAdminClaims (replaces Firebase ID token in lib/api.js)

implemented.name: aiProxy
implemented.implementation: lib/ai/proxy.js — one call to one NAMED provider via router.callProvider, so it neither falls through the preference order nor honours the AI feature switches: an administrator testing configuration must not be answered by a different provider, and a switched-off feature must stay diagnosable. Returns 200 with ok:false on a provider error rather than 5xx, because an unconfigured provider is an answer. Writes an ai_usage record, which nothing had written since the port.

implemented.name: testAiProvider
implemented.implementation: lib/ai/proxy.js — sends a one-word prompt to the named provider and writes status/latencyMs/lastTested back onto its ai_providers document, which the portal's status badge has always read and nothing had ever set.

implemented.name: mcpProxy
implemented.implementation: functions/src/functions/mcp-http.js + lib/ai/mcp.js — Entra editor-gated server-side MCP tools/call proxy. Credentials resolve from Azure Function App settings / Key Vault references or the write-only Cosmos oauthToken field; supports Streamable HTTP and the seeded SSE transport.

implemented.name: syncMcpTools
implemented.implementation: functions/src/functions/mcp-http.js + lib/ai/mcp.js — Entra editor-gated server-side tools/list call. Normalizes and stores the tool manifest in Cosmos, records connected/error status, and never returns credentials.

implemented.name: publerProxy
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/rest-proxy.js — authenticated pass-through to Publer at https://app.publer.com/api/v1, credentialed from PUBLER_API_KEY + PUBLER_WORKSPACE_ID. The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected.

implemented.name: klaviyoProxy
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/rest-proxy.js — authenticated pass-through to Klaviyo at https://a.klaviyo.com, credentialed from KLAVIYO_PRIVATE_KEY. The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected.

implemented.name: linkieProxy
implemented.implementation: lib/integrations/rest-proxy.js — authenticated pass-through to Linkie at https://app.linkie.bio/api/v1 (LINKIE_API_BASE_URL overridable), credentialed from LINKIE_API_KEY. The caller supplies {path, method, body}; assertSafePath is the security boundary, rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, schemes, '..' segments, backslashes and control characters, because a credentialed proxy with a caller-chosen path is a confused deputy and the gate in front is 'editor', not 'admin'. Upstream status and body are passed through so the admin page can show the real error. An unseeded key returns 200 with ok:false and INTEGRATION_NOT_CONFIGURED, which the Connections page renders as not-connected. Additionally allowlisted to the endpoints the admin page calls — /profiles, /analytics/traffic-stats and the profile-scoped posts routes — because the API key's scopes are broader than any one screen needs. Base URL and allowlist taken from Site-Main functions/cms/proxies.js rather than inferred.

implemented.name: generateArticleDraft
implemented.collection: (none — returns the draft; persisting is the caller's Stage 4 createContentItem)
implemented.implementation: lib/content/draft-from-url.js — scrape the primary URL (lib/content/scrape.js, direct + env-gated reader/headless fallbacks), fold extra KB article URLs (scraped, max 3), server-fetched documentUrls (PDF→base64 / inline text, 3 MB / 15 s caps) and uploaded supportingDocuments into the drafter's 5-document ceiling, then one createDrafter().generateDraft call — the same drafter the forge and digest use, feature-gated as forgeDrafting. Accepts both callers' payload dialects: the Publish-Ready Builder's {url, urls, cloudProvider, customInstructionPrompt, documentUrls, supportingDocuments} and the editor's {url, cloudProvider, draftText, instructions}. Editor-gated; 75 s internal budget under the client's 90 s timeout, mapping 400 bad URL / 422 unscrapeable / 504 budget / 502 generation so the UI shows the real reason. Response { ok, draft: { title, summary, postContent, summaryPrompt, detailsPrompt, keyTopics, suggestedContentType, sourceUrls } }.

implemented.name: getForgeConfig
implemented.implementation: lib/content/forge-studio.js — the Forge Studio read: both voice documents run through the same normalizers the pipeline trusts (normalizeProfile/normalizePrompts, so the Studio edits exactly what the forge reads back), the calibration suggestions (sanitized, capped), the FORMAT_LIBRARY summary and the forge_stats scoreboard. Editor-gated.

implemented.name: updateForgeConfig
implemented.implementation: lib/content/forge-studio.js — whitelist-validated partial update of forge_profile (certifications, speakingTopics, interestAreas, wordSoup ≤20k chars, suggestion accept/dismiss trims) and forge_prompts (masterPrompt, extraBannedPhrases, styleRules, publishThreshold, autoForge; version incremented). Unknown fields are dropped, not stored; values pass through the pipeline's own normalizers before writing. Audited to admin_audit_logs as forge_config_updated; clears the in-process forge-config cache (other warm workers converge within the 5-minute TTL). Returns the fresh getForgeConfig payload. Editor-gated.

notImplemented.description: Functions the frontend invokes TODAY that have no registered route — every call is a live 404 in the admin UI. Kept out of 'implemented' so the gap is visible and machine-checked (functions/src/functions/api-contract.test.js asserts functions = implemented + notImplemented exactly, and that none of these is registered). Implementing one of these REQUIRES moving it to 'implemented' in the same change, or the contract test fails.
notImplemented.blockedOn: Provider credentials — TODO.md (OpenAI/Anthropic keys, Klaviyo/Publer/Linkie tokens). The route scaffolding is not the blocker; shipping a proxy with nowhere to proxy to would be a 502 instead of a 404.

realtime.rationale: All realtime consumers are admin surfaces with one operator. Cosmos change feed cannot be subscribed from a browser. Poll intervals of 10-30s match the labs agent's own pollFallbackIntervalMs design and add no moving parts.

limits.messagesPerDay: 20000 HARD CAP - no overage purchasable; delivery simply stops for the rest of the day

signalrOption.fitAssessment: 20 connections is ample for a single-operator admin. The 20k/day cap is the constraint: a 1 msg/sec stream exhausts it in ~5.5h, so it only fits EVENT-DRIVEN pushes (Cosmos change feed -> Functions output binding -> push on actual data change), never chatty streams.
cautions: Free -> Standard scaling incurs downtime: the public IP changes, 30-60 min DNS propagation
Standard_S1 (~$49/unit/month) is a third of the USD 150 platform ceiling and is NOT justified by one admin's dashboard
no SLA means the realtime layer can degrade with no recourse - polling fallback must remain in the client regardless
signalrOption.adoptionTrigger: only if polling proves sluggish in practice; ship polling first

authMigration.to: MSAL (lib/msalConfig.js already present) acquiring a token for entra_api_audience; lib/api.js swaps token source and base URL (VITE_GCP_FUNCTIONS_URL -> VITE_AZURE_FUNCTIONS_URL)
authMigration.note: verify-token.js on the backend already validates aud against the API registration — DECISION 3

storageMigration.to: Functions endpoints owning all blob access. Uploads are base64 JSON through POST cms/uploads/{container}; downloads are served by GET public/media/{container}/{*blobPath} through the Function App's managed identity. The SAS design described here was NOT built: the storage account is closed to the internet and allow_nested_items_to_be_public is false, so a browser-held SAS would have had nothing to talk to (TODO.md T-105). generateSasUrl still exists for server-side use and signs with a user delegation key.
storageMigration.note: the Function App identity already holds Storage Blob Data Contributor on the content account
